case.case_title: Deshapriya v. Rukmani, Divisional Secretary, Dodangoda and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1999] 2 Sri LR 412

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the suspension of the petitioner was discriminatory on the ground of political opinion, violating Article 12(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his suspension was due to hostile discrimination because he refused to support the People's Alliance and was a supporter of a rival political party (JVP).
case_context.respondent_argument: The 2nd respondent denied knowledge but admitted acting on orders; the 3rd respondent's letter confirmed the suspension was politically motivated.
key_facts: Petitioner refused to canvass for People's Alliance candidates.
3rd respondent reported petitioner as supporting JVP and requested disciplinary action.
Suspension was a result of political discrimination.
Use of state resources for partisan political purposes was established.
Petitioner was the only Samurdhi Niyamaka suspended for political dissent.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(2) as prohibiting discrimination on political opinion, including the misuse of state resources to benefit one political party over others.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The suspension was motivated by the petitioner's political opinion and refusal to support the ruling party's candidates, constituting hostile discrimination in violation of Article 12(2).
principles_established: Political discrimination by state actors violates Article 12(2).
Use of public resources for partisan political advantage is unequal treatment.
Democracy requires protection and tolerance of lawful dissent.

outcome.holding: The court held that the 2nd and 3rd respondents infringed the petitioner's fundamental right under Article 12(2) by politically discriminating against him.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The suspension was declared null and void; compensation was awarded to the petitioner, with personal liability on the 2nd and 3rd respondents.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was central because the suspension was directly caused by political discrimination, violating the petitioner's constitutional protection against such discrimination.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The 3rd respondent's letter confirmed the suspension was due to the petitioner's political opinion and refusal to support the ruling party, constituting hostile discrimination.
